1: I saw today how the light through the window scattered onto the shelf of jars. Each jar seemed to whisper its own name. I labeled them with ink, but they seem to have written an answer back.
2: Mom, there's some kind of mold or something in the bathtub, the smell is just terrible. We probably need to call someone. Come take a look, and don't forget to cover your nose.
3: My grandmother's best mushroom soup recipe: We will need: chanterelles, black pepper, porcini, onion, mycelium, hand, mycelium, mycelium, mycelium, myce... [illegible]
4: The best daily routine for successful people: 1. Wake up 2. Take a shit 3. Get out of bed 4. ... [illegible]
5: I left a piece of bread on the table today. An hour later, it was smiling. I don't know from whom, but I smiled back.
6: Problem with the bathroom floor: something is swelling under the tiles. At first it seems small, then movement is visible.
7: A small white dot was found on the table today. Don't touch it with your hands — just watch.
8: If someone comes into the basement, let them leave the door ajar for an hour — the air must not stagnate.
9: New mold has appeared on the south wall of the basement. Looks like little caps, as if someone left them there on purpose. The smell is pungent, but not too strong. Keep the door closed until we figure out where it came from.
10: Found an old mug with tea stains in the kitchen. It smells like yesterday's rain and old wood. Hard to say why it's so comforting.
11: This morning I noticed the shadow from the lamp stretching across the floor. It almost moved on its own, as if it were watching me.
12: A new sound appeared in the hallway. A creak. Long. I don't understand where from. Need to check the floorboards, but carefully.
13: Made a long shopping list today. First the usual things: bread, milk, butter, onion, carrots, potatoes. Then I remembered I needed garlic, it's almost gone. And rice, some pasta. Then I thought I should get tea and coffee, though they might not be in stock. And a few cans of food, but which ones — I don't know, have to choose carefully to last a long time. Then a pen for notes and paper, just in case, because everything you write on the wall gradually washes away. And candles, and matches. And batteries too. Although, it doesn't really matter, none of us have long left anyway.
14: Checked the kitchen cabinets today. Some spice jars had shifted slightly, though I definitely didn't touch them. An old piece of bread lay on the top shelf — seemed dry, but [illegible] were moving on their own... [illegible].
15: Patient: male, approximately 42 years old. Symptoms: weakness, fever, dry cough, occasional slight trembling of the hands. Observations: skin appears pale with a slight grayish tint; shallow breathing. Eyes react to light normally, but the gaze is vacant, as if trying to remember something long forgotten.
16: Recommendations: limit contact with others, provide plenty of [illegible], observe every three hours. And, to be honest, sometimes it feels like we are observing not just the patient, but whatever is [illegible] inside.
17: It doesn't look like a common cold. Possibly the start of the [illegible] I've heard about in other cities. Unclear if it's airborne or through contact with something in the house. The patient says little, answers are short, almost detached. Sometimes [illegible], but the eyes are empty.
18: Hi, Helen. Don't forget to return my bread knife, the one with the wooden handle. I'm sure I left it on the shelf, but now I can't find it. And if you can, take the jar of coffee with you, it's been sitting on my table for a week... [illegible].
19: Mike, remember you left a book of notes at my place? Try to pick it up by tomorrow. I can't open it myself right now — the cabinet keys are lost. And be careful with the pages, some of them are damp... [illegible].
20: Dear Tina. Please return your owl-pattern mug. It's in the kitchen by the window, and I keep mixing it up with mine. Thanks... [illegible].
21: Kevin, left a couple of cans of food on the windowsill for you. Don't forget to grab them, or the mold will find its way quickly... although, maybe it's already too late.
22: Sarah, remember that notebook I gave you for notes? Return it, please, when you can. There are a few important thoughts and... [illegible], I can't even make out what's written there myself anymore.
23: Checked the old stove in the kitchen today. The problem is the door is sticking and the fire won't stay lit. Need to tighten the hinges, grease them with something fatty.
24: The kitchen faucet leaks constantly. Tried tightening it, but the water still drips. Seems like the washer is worn out. Need to find a replacement... though, maybe it's just a sound, not water.
25: The old flashlight barely works. The batteries are weak. If you want to use it, you need to clean the contacts and try another power source. The instructions seem simple, but sometimes it feels like the light itself decides when to turn on... [illegible]
26: I try to go to bed at the same time. Sometimes the clock runs too fast, sometimes too slow. Sometimes it seems the room itself adjusts to my sleep.
27: Every morning I check the windows, radiators, and doors. Even if everything is fine, I do it again. I don't know why, just a habit. Sometimes I hear a soft creak, as if the house itself is reminding me of its presence.
28: Today is Thursday. It feels like two days have passed since I wrote down yesterday's observations, but in reality, it's been longer. Sometimes time feels like a liquid, and sometimes like concrete.
29: I count the days in my notebook. Every day I put a checkmark. But sometimes the checkmarks disappear, even though I definitely put them there.
30: Friday. It feels like the week didn't move, and then suddenly a leap. Sometimes I mark dates just to remember that I'm still alive. Sometimes it feels like the calendar is whispering.
31: The diary says 'Tuesday,' but the light outside is different, the noise is strange, as if yesterday mixed with today...
32: Today I checked the electrical system in the kitchen. The ceiling light flickered five times in a row, and after that, the light became weak, as if the bulb itself was tired of shining. Decided to remove the cover and check the wires: the insulation is old, cracked in places, and one wire looked completely bare. Tried tightening the contacts and greasing them with oil leftovers from a jar on the windowsill. The flashlight doesn't work either — the batteries are almost dead and the contacts are oxidized. Interestingly, the flashlight sometimes lights up even when I don't turn it on. Yesterday it flashed once, today — twice. Can't tell if it's a coincidence or if it's trying to say something.
33: Every morning I do the same thing. First I check the windows, then the doors, then the radiators and shelves. The mug on the table is always in the same spot, the spoon lies perfectly straight beside it. If anything shifts, the day feels wrong. Today I noticed the tea smells different than yesterday: a bit sharper, as if a foreign scent was added. Don't know who or what could have done it. I counted all the spoons and forks three times — the first time there were 12, the second — 11, the third — 12. It seems the things are whispering among themselves. Sometimes I think I'm losing the sense of where habit ends and something living begins.
34: There's a notebook on the table. Don't open it until I get back; there are entries there that are better not read aloud.
35: I went out into the field behind the house, but the grass has grown so high that I can no longer see the horizon, and the ground beneath my feet squelched as if it wasn't mud, but someone's tongue.
36: I brought her a flower, but it withered in a second, and its petals turned into dry skin that crumbled right in my palms.
37: The grass by the doorstep moves even in total calm, and yesterday I noticed it slowly growing through the door crack right into the hallway.
38: Yesterday a bird hit my window, but instead of falling, it stuck to the glass and began to slowly absorb into the room.
39: A fish died in the aquarium, but it continues to swim belly-up, opening its mouth and trying to pronounce my name — I can clearly hear it.
40: My dog has been staring at an empty corner and growling for three hours, but I see no one there, except for a long shadow that doesn't belong to the furniture.
41: A horse stood on the road, completely motionless, and when I got closer, it turned out that instead of eyes, it had ordinary door peepholes inserted.
42: The neighbor's cow wandered into our yard, and its mooing sounded like the cry of a small child lost in a thick fog.
43: The milk in the fridge turned into a thick red substance overnight, but it still tasted like childhood and metal.
44: The bread on the table became covered in black spots that form a map of the city, and if you press the center, a soft scream comes from the loaf.
45: This cheese smells like something unfresh, almost human, and when I cut a piece, the edge of the cut slowly heals like a wound.
46: Grandma's soup tastes strangely bitter today, and at the bottom of the plate, I found a copper ring that my father lost ten years ago in the forest.
47: The porridge in the pot bubbles as if it's trying to breathe, and every popping bubble whispers: 'not yet time, not yet time.'
48: The tea cooled instantly, and a film formed on the surface where I saw a reflection of the room, with someone standing behind my back.
49: The coffee is so black today that it absorbs the lamplight, and I'm afraid to look into the cup for fear of seeing the bottom of the abyss.
50: I poured sugar into the cup, but the grains started crawling across the table, forming lines in a language unknown to me.
51: Salt spilled on the floor, and I didn't clean it up — they say it protects against those who walk behind the walls, but they still scratch.
52: Pepper got in my eyes, and for a moment the world turned crimson, and all the people in the room turned into tall black pillars of smoke.
53: The plate cracked on its own right in my hands, and the break was perfectly even, revealing someone's gray hair inside the porcelain.
54: The spoon reflects my face, but in the reflection, I look much older and my lips are sewn shut with thick, coarse thread.
55: The fork plunged into the table so deeply that I can't pull it out, and thick black tar began to ooze from the hole.
56: The kitchen knife has become so sharp that it cuts the air, leaving thin black slits that draw in the cold of the dungeon.
57: The pot on the stove is full of boiling water, but the steam doesn't rise; it crawls across the floor, filling the room with thick gray fog.
58: The frying pan glowed white-hot even though the stove was off, and a silhouette of someone's face distorted in a scream appeared on its bottom.
59: The stove makes a strange clicking sound, the rhythm of which suspiciously matches Morse code, but I'm afraid to translate the message.
60: The refrigerator hums so loudly that I can't hear my own thoughts, and when it goes silent, a dead silence falls over the house.
61: This room seems smaller than it was yesterday — I measured the distance between the walls, and it has shrunk by exactly three inches.
62: The kitchen has become a place where time stands still: the clocks here are stopped, and the water in the tap flows upward, contrary to all laws of nature.
63: The bathtub filled itself with dark water smelling of rust, and at the bottom, I could see the outlines of something very long and many-legged.
64: The bed creaks under my weight even when I'm not lying on it, and in the mornings, I find someone else's clipped fingernails on the sheets.
65: The pillow has become heavy as a stone, and inside it, something is rhythmically thumping like a tiny mechanical heart.
66: The blanket chokes me at night, tightening around my neck, and it seems that someone cold and very thin is hiding under it.
67: The closet in the bedroom is locked, but from inside comes the constant scratching of claws on wood and quiet pleas to be let out.
68: The mirror no longer shows my reflection — it only shows an empty room with an open door, which someone is entering.
69: The clock started running backward, and with every turn of the hands, I feel important pieces of my life disappearing from my memory.
70: The lamp blinks in a certain rhythm, and if you look at it long enough, you can see scenes from your future that are better left unknown.
71: The computer turned on by itself in the middle of the night and displayed only one message: 'I see you through the camera, even when it's taped over.'
72: The keyboard is sticky to the touch, and some keys won't press, as if something living and soft is stuck underneath them.
73: The mouse moves across the pad on its own, drawing circles, and the cursor on the monitor circles my eyes on an old digital photo.
74: The monitor screen has become mirrored, and I see in it not myself, but the one sitting directly behind my back in this very chair.
75: The internet is full of sites that don't exist, and on one of them, I found a live stream from my own bedroom.
76: The program issued a critical error, the code of which translates into text as 'Help me, it's very dark and cold here.'
77: The file with my documents turned into a set of strange symbols that begin to bleed directly onto the paper when printed.
78: The 'Personal' folder turned out to be empty, although I clearly remember storing all my memories there — now they are gone from my head too.
79: The data on the disk is corrupted beyond recovery, and every time I try to restore it, the computer emits an agonizing human wail.
80: The server in the basement overheated, and it smells like burnt wool, even though ice water is circulating in the cooling system.
81: Working in this office is driving me crazy: colleagues come and go, but I've never seen their faces — only the backs of their heads.
82: The money in my wallet turned into dry fallen leaves, but they accepted them at the store as if they were large bills.
83: The project for the new hospital I was working on began to change shape on the blueprints, turning into a tangled, endless labyrinth.
84: The idea came to me in a dream: I just need to sew up all the windows and doors, then the city won't be able to get inside my house.
85: Today's task is simple: reach the end of the hallway without turning back to the whisper calling my name from the darkness.
86: The solution was found too late — the lock on the front door has disappeared, and now I am forever trapped in this distorted reality.
87: The question is not how I got here, but why the shadow I cast has started living a life of its own.
88: The answer came in the form of a note under the door, written in my handwriting: 'Run while you still remember your name.'
89: Time flows strangely here: I blinked, and a whole summer flew by outside the window, while the snow on the windowsill never melted.
90: The date on the calendar is frozen on October 31, and no matter how many pages I tear off, the same day is always underneath.
91: A year ago I stepped into this fog, and since then I haven't seen the sun, only this eternal gray twilight and silhouettes in the distance.
92: Month after month I wander these streets, and each time I return to the same house with broken windows.
93: A week has passed since I last ate, but I feel no hunger, only an endless void somewhere in my chest.
94: Day turned to night in mere seconds, and the darkness here is so thick you could cut it with a knife — it settles on the skin like soot.
95: Morning brought no relief: the fog only grew thicker, and the siren sounds in the distance became much closer and clearer.
96: Evening is the most dangerous time, when shadows lengthen and begin to detach from the walls, crawling across the floor toward my bed.
97: The night never ends, and I hear someone huge slowly tossing and turning under the floor, shaking the whole house.
98: Holidays in this city are celebrated strangely: people wear masks made of real skin and dance around bonfires made of old furniture.
99: Joy is a forgotten feeling that I experienced when I found a rusty key, but it didn't fit any of the doors in this house.
100: Success is near: I've almost reached the lighthouse, but the ground beneath my feet is turning to ash, and I fear this is also just a dream.
101: Yesterday I tried to call the elevator, but instead of the cabin, an empty shaft arrived, filled with children's laughter and the smell of damp earth.
102: Instruction for residents: if you hear crying behind the wall, don't try to comfort the neighbor — no one has lived in our building for five years.
103: My keys have become soft as wax; I try to insert them into the lock, but they just smear across the keyhole.
104: Found an old photo: I'm standing next to someone whose face is blacked out with a marker, but that someone is holding me by the throat.
105: The rain outside is not falling down, but up, and the sky looks solid, as if it's not clouds, but a dirty concrete ceiling.
106: In the first-aid kit, instead of pills, I found small dried eyes — the label says 'take in case of hallucinations.'
107: The bedroom window now faces a brick wall, even though I live on the tenth floor and yesterday the whole city was visible there.
108: My pulse has slowed to one beat per minute, but I feel surprisingly alert, as if I no longer need blood.
109: The TV only shows static, but if you look long enough, you can make out a floor plan of my apartment with crosses marking certain spots.
110: I found a finger in the mailbox, wrapped in a thirty-year-old newspaper — it's wearing my wedding ring.
111: Every word I speak aloud falls to the floor like a heavy stone; I'm afraid to talk, so as not to fill the room completely.
112: A stranger's towel is hanging in the bathroom; it's always warm and damp, as if it was just used to wipe something very hot and sticky.
113: The neighbor came by for salt, but when he smiled, I noticed he had two rows of teeth and all of them were molars.
114: The phone book is filled with the names of people who have gone missing in this county over the last half-century.
115: My shadow has started lagging behind my movements by a couple of seconds, and sometimes it makes gestures that I didn't make.
116: The ceiling is slowly lowering; every day I get a little closer to the chandelier, and soon I'll have to crawl.
117: Yesterday I found a human fingernail in my soup; it was painted with the same polish my late mother used.
118: I opened my umbrella, but rusty fishing hooks showered out of it and dug into my shoulders.
119: The walls in the hallway are covered in tiny pores, and sometimes transparent sweat oozes from them, smelling of fear.
120: I set the alarm for seven in the morning, but it went off yesterday evening, and a voice from the speaker said: 'You're already late.'
121: In the kitchen drawer, all the forks are bent at a ninety-degree angle, as if someone tried to make tiny ladders out of them.
122: The doorbell rings every time I close my eyes, but only an empty fog stands behind the door.
123: I found my father's diary: the last hundred pages are filled with sketches of the same long, faceless creature.
124: The tap water smells of old coins and iodine; after washing, dark spots remain on my face that won't wash off.
125: My slippers are in different corners of the room every morning, as if they tried to run away from this house during the night.
126: The radio picks up signals from the cemetery: whispered names and dates that haven't happened yet.
127: In the freezer among the vegetables, I found my own heart, frozen in a block of ice — it's still faintly pulsing.
128: I tried to write a letter, but the pen only writes in red, even though the ink in it was always blue.
129: The lamp in the living room sways on its own, and its shadow resembles a gallows-man slowly circling in the void.
130: A crow with human lips sits on the windowsill and whispers to me: 'The door isn't locked, come in.'
131: Music from a music box is playing in my head, and I can't remember the last time I heard silence.
132: I looked through the peephole and saw myself standing on the other side of the door, begging to be let in.
133: The dust in this room consists of skin scales and ground bones; I inhale dead people with every breath.
134: Someone scratched on the toilet wall: 'There is no exit here, only new entrances.'
135: The curtains on the windows are constantly moving, as if someone is hiding behind them, but there's only empty glass and an endless gray day.
136: I found an old music player; in the headphones, I can hear the screams of people drowning in something thick and sweet.
137: The ventilation in the house spreads the smell of rotten apples and formalin; I think someone is stuck in the pipes.
138: My fingernails have started growing into my fingers; it causes terrible pain, but the doctors say it's a normal stage of transformation.
139: I drew a circle with chalk around the bed, but in the morning I found the chalk had turned into a chain of tiny teeth.
140: In the oven, I found a child's shoe, half-burned but still warm inside.
141: The reflection in the window doesn't match what I see in the mirror: in the window, I look like a formless heap of meat.
142: The postage stamps on the envelopes depict torture scenes, but no one but me notices.
143: I found an old mannequin in the basement; every time I return, it stands one step closer to the exit.
144: The hair in the sink weaves into complex knots that resemble a map of constellations that aren't in the sky.
145: I tried to leave the city by the highway, but after an hour of driving, I found myself back at my apartment building.
146: A plate of soup has been sitting on the dining table for a month, but it's still hot and steaming.
147: The bedroom walls have become soft to the touch, and if I press harder, I can feel muscles rolling under the wallpaper.
148: I found an old newspaper: the headline says I died in a car accident ten years ago.
149: The cat brought me not a mouse, but a tiny human hand in its teeth, still clutching a small scrap of paper.
150: The light bulbs in the hallway explode one by one as I pass by, leaving me in absolute darkness with whatever is following me.
151: My teeth have started to loosen, and when one fell out, I saw that the root looked like a tiny bony finger.
152: At the bottom of my coffee cup, I saw my own face, but it was screaming in pain, even though I was silent at that moment.
153: The trees in the yard have lost their bark; now they look like huge exposed nerves, trembling in the wind.
154: I found an old coat in the closet; in the pockets were keys to houses that no longer exist on the map.
155: Every time I blink, the furniture in the room slightly changes its position, slowly surrounding me.
156: The bathroom mirror fogged up, and someone wrote from the inside: 'I see you, but you don't see me.'
157: I hear huge mechanisms humming underground, as if this whole city is just a stage set on a giant machine.
158: My skin has become transparent, and I can see my veins pulsing with a black liquid that looks like oil.
159: Yesterday I found a staircase that only leads down; I descended it for three hours but never found the bottom.
160: The phone in the hallway only gives a long dial tone, which gradually turns into an ultrasonic shriek that makes the vessels in my eyes burst.
161: Crumbs appeared on the kitchen table, forming my name; I live alone and haven't eaten bread in a week.
162: I opened a book to a random page, and the letters began to fall off the sheet, turning into small black insects.
163: There are statues in the park that change poses when you're not looking — yesterday one was pointing at my window.
164: The smell of burning follows me everywhere, though there are no fires in the city, and the sky is covered in eternal fog.
165: I found an old film in the basement: it shows me sleeping in this very room, with something long standing over me.
166: My ears filled with cotton, but I still hear a voice whispering: 'Your time is almost up, get ready.'
167: The water in the toilet rose and splashed hundreds of old, rusted wedding rings onto the floor.
168: I tried to scream, but instead of a voice, a swarm of gray moths flew out of my mouth and immediately covered the lamp.
169: On an old map of the city, I found an area marked as 'Place for those who have stopped hoping.'
170: Yesterday I saw the sun rise in the west, but it wasn't golden; it was deathly pale, like a corpse's face.
171: The pot on the stove began to make sounds like deep throat-singing in a forgotten language.
172: I found a note in my pocket: 'Don't trust mirrors; they don't show what is real, but what you want to hide.'
173: There are no children in this city, but on the playgrounds, the swings are constantly moving, as if invisible heavy beings are sitting on them.
174: My handwriting has started to change: now I write in letters that look like intertwined bones and barbed wire.
175: In the hospital basement, I found a ward where instead of beds, there are giant iron cages with doctors' names on them.
176: I stepped in a puddle, but it turned out to be bottomless; I barely managed to pull my leg out before I was sucked down.
177: Yesterday I met a woman who had smooth skin instead of a face, but she recognized me and called me by name.
178: Old newspapers in this city are always dated tomorrow and always describe someone's death.
179: A wet spot in the shape of a human silhouette appeared on the kitchen ceiling, and it's slowly increasing in size.
180: I found an abandoned altar in the woods, on which lay my childhood toy, covered in old dried blood.
181: Every time I lock the door, I hear someone on the other side trying the handle and sighing in disappointment.
182: My bones have started making a strange ringing sound when I walk, as if they are made of hollow porcelain, not organic matter.
183: In the fridge, I found a jar labeled 'Your last words,' but it was absolutely empty.
184: The fog outside has become so thick that I can no longer see my own hands when I stretch them out in front of me.
185: I found a strand of hair in an old dresser that began to squirm in my hands, trying to wrap around my fingers.
186: In this city, all doors only open one way — into the darkness from which no one returns.
187: I saw a giant shadow fly across the sky that had no body, and after that, all the birds in the forest went silent forever.
188: My watch stopped, but I continue to hear its ticking, which now comes from somewhere under my skin.
189: I found an old MRI scan: instead of a brain, the patient's scan showed a coiled snake.
190: The walls in this house remember all my sins, and at night they start playing them back to me as shadows on the ceiling.
191: I found a doll in the attic that looks exactly like me, and there's a real needle stuck in its chest.
192: Yesterday I tried to wash my face, but hot ash showered out of the tap, burning my face and hands.
193: Inscriptions made in blood appeared on the living room wallpaper, but they disappear as soon as I turn on a bright light.
194: I hear someone moving furniture in the empty room next door and humming my mother's lullaby.
195: There is no exit in this city, only an eternal repetition of the same nightmare in which I always lose.
196: I found a well in the woods that smells of fresh-baked bread and rotting meat at the same time.
197: My reflection in the mirror began to age before my eyes until it turned into a skeleton that continued to smile at me.
198: I found a message in a bottle washed up on the lakeshore: it contained my address and the date of my death today.
199: The streetlights turned purple, and in that light, I saw that all the shadows in the city lead to the same building.
200: I finally realized that I am not a guest here, but part of this distorted reality, and the fog is my only home.
201: Today I found an old projector in the attic. When I turned it on, the frames flickering on the sheet weren't from my life: I saw myself as a child standing in the middle of a burning field, but instead of my parents, two tall figures in faceless medical coats were holding my hands. The strangest thing is that on the film, you can hear my present-day self breathing right behind that child's back, and he turns around, looking exactly into the lens, as if he sees me across the decades.
202: A note found in the abandoned hospital registry: 'The patient from room 304 claims that his body is just a suit sewn from someone else's memories. Yesterday he started ripping the seams on his stomach to show us the "true contents," but instead of organs, old rusty keys to the Lakeside Motel fell out of the wound. We locked him in, but this morning the room was empty, and only neatly folded skin lay on the bed.'
203: Radio operating manual: 'If you catch frequency 104.2, do not try to turn the dial further. The voice you hear will belong to your late wife. She will beg you to come to the amusement park. Remember: whatever she says, do not ask her what the earth smells like. If you do, the radio will start to bleed, and you will never be able to turn off the sound again, even if you pull the plug from the socket.'
204: I spent all day trying to scrub the mold in the bathroom, but it behaves like a living thing. The moment I turn away, it arranges itself into complex geometric patterns resembling a map of constellations found in no atlas. And when I bring a sponge to it, it starts to pulsate and emit a sound like a very fast, panicked heartbeat. It seems it isn't growing on the wall, but growing out from inside the house itself, using the concrete as a nutrient medium.
205: Diary of an anonymous worker: 'The city council ordered us to board up all the basements on South Vale. They said it was because of a sewage leak, but I heard what's down there. It’s not the sound of water. It’s the sound of millions of tiny legs running across metal. Yesterday, one of our guys, Bill, dropped his flashlight down the shaft and climbed in after it. We pulled him out five minutes later, but he was completely white-haired and claimed there is no bottom, only an endless hall full of people glued to the ceiling.'
206: An echo has taken up residence in my refrigerator. Every time I open the door, I hear a fragment of a conversation that took place here years ago. Today it was my voice, arguing with someone about buying train tickets. But I never bought tickets, and I never lived in this apartment before last month. The most frightening part is that the voice in the echo sounds as if my mouth is full of sand, and I'm choking on every word.
207: Found an old Polaroid photo on the street. It depicts my house, but all the windows have been replaced with giant human eyes. At first I thought it was some stupid edit, but when I looked at my house just now, I noticed the window frames have become soft and moist, and behind the glass, giant pupils are slowly moving, following my every step on the sidewalk. I'm afraid to go inside — what if the house decides to blink while I'm in the doorway?
208: Police officer's report: 'Arrived on a noise complaint at house No. 12 on Sanders Street. The door was open. Inside, we found a dining table set for twelve. All the food was made of wax but looked terrifyingly realistic. The owner of the house sat in the center, sewn to the chair with thin wire. When asked what was happening, he replied that he was waiting for the shadows to finish their dance. We found no shadows until we turned off the light.'
209: I've started to notice that my height changes depending on my mood. When I'm scared, the hallways become infinitely long and the ceiling vanishes into the stratosphere, turning me into a tiny insect. But when I'm angry, the room shrinks, the walls press against my shoulders, and I feel my bones cracking as they try to fit into this small concrete box. Today I feel complete indifference, and it seems I've just started to dissolve into the air, becoming transparent like the morning fog outside the window.
210: A letter I found under the mat: 'Dear John, if you're reading this, it means you forgot to take your pills again. Look at your hands. See those red lines? They aren't veins. They are the strings the city uses to pull you. You think you’re going to the kitchen for water of your own free will, but you’re actually just following a programmed algorithm. To be free, you need to find a knife and cut the thickest string behind your left ear. Don't fear the pain; the real pain is continuing to be a puppet in this foggy theater.'
211: Today at the store I tried to buy bread, but the clerk demanded my happiest memory instead of money. He said coins have no value here anymore; only emotions frozen in time matter. I tried to remember my tenth birthday, but found only a gray hole in my head. It seems I’ve already paid with that memory for something else I can't recall. He ended up giving me a stale crust in exchange for the name of my first love.
212: A note on a public restroom mirror: 'The one standing behind you in the mirror is not your enemy. He just wants to switch places. He’s tired of watching your boring life from the cold looking-glass. All he has there are endless tiled hallways and the smell of bleach. Let him out. Just press your forehead against the glass and don't close your eyes until you feel your feet becoming cold and flat. It’s a small price to pay for never having to feel fear again.'
213: I found an old city phone book, and all the numbers in it lead to the same place — the local hospital morgue. I called one at random, and I was the one who picked up, but my voice sounded as if I were underwater. That other me said: "It’s not so bad here, just very quiet. Come over, I've cleared the neighboring shelf for you. It’s warm because someone who really wanted to live was just lying here."
214: In Rosewater Park, I saw a man feeding pigeons scraps of his old photographs. The birds greedily pecked at the paper, and I noticed that with every piece eaten, the man became less distinct, his outlines blurring until he turned into a translucent smudge. The pigeons, conversely, began to take on human features — they had the faces of his relatives, and they began whispering among themselves, discussing his mistakes.
215: My apartment has started generating electricity from my nightmares. Last night, when I dreamed I was suffocating in a coffin, all the light bulbs in the house flared with a blinding white light, and the TV began broadcasting a recording of my scream at full volume. I woke up in a cold sweat, but the light didn't go out. It turns out that for the house to stay lit, I must constantly have bad dreams. The city won't let me sleep peacefully; it uses my anxiety as fuel.
216: Found an abandoned mailbox in the woods, stuffed to the brim with letters to God. They are all written on human skin and smell of burnt hair. One was open, and it said: "Lord, if you hear us, please make the fog stop imitating the voices of our children. We know they are dead, but it’s so hard not to open the door when you hear 'Daddy, I'm cold' right outside the threshold." There was no signature, only a bloody palm print.
217: In the library, I found a book titled "The History of Your Disappearance." It details everything I’ve done for the last three days, including my thoughts of ending it all. The last page isn't finished yet; letters are slowly appearing on it: "He stands at the bookshelf reading these lines, unaware that the librarian has already locked the exit and begun to turn into something long and hungry." I'm afraid to turn around.
218: Today the radio broadcast the weather forecast: 'Expect brief showers of teeth and a moderate wind bringing the scent of old sins. By evening, hallucinations in the form of deceased relatives are possible. Please stay home and do not look into mirrors when the lights are off. The city administration reminds you: your madness is your personal responsibility; do not burden the surrounding shadows with it.'
219: I found a jar in the kitchen labeled "Silence." When I opened it, all the sounds in the world instantly vanished. I couldn't hear my own breathing, my heartbeat, even the sound of a shattering plate was absolutely silent. It was bliss for the first ten minutes, but then I started hearing what sounds *inside* the silence — a low-frequency hum, like the chewing of giant jaws. It turns out the sounds of our world just hide the noise of hell's own machinery from us.
220: A note on the door of an empty apartment: 'We left because the walls started telling the truth. It turns out the house hates us for walking on its floors and breathing its air. It said it would eat our dog if we weren't out by sunset. We didn't believe it, but in the evening we found only a collar and a pile of old buttons in the bowl. Don't enter here if there is even a drop of affection for any living thing in your heart.'
221: Yesterday I found an old sewing machine in the basement. It was working on its own, stitching together pieces of old clothes and newspaper clippings. As I moved closer, I saw it was sewing a flag for a country that doesn't exist. The flag depicts a black circle on a gray background, and such a cold emanates from the image that my eyelashes froze. It seems this machine is sewing a shroud for this entire city, stitch by stitch bringing the finale closer.
222: My reflection in a puddle this morning was a few seconds faster than me. I was just about to lift my foot, but it had already taken a step forward. At one point it stopped, looked at me with deep contempt, and walked into the depths of the dark water, leaving me standing without a shadow or a double. Now I feel half empty, as if an important part of my consciousness simply decided it didn't want to go my way anymore.
223: The local bar, "Heaven's Night," serves a drink called "Oblivion." The bartender says one sip makes you forget the worst day of your life. I drank a whole glass, but instead of forgetting anything, I began to remember the lives of every person who had sat at that bar before me. Now my head holds thousands of deaths, thousands of betrayals, and one endless scream that doesn't quiet down even when I try to sleep.
224: Instruction for those lost in the fog: '1. Do not try to navigate by instruments; they point toward your fear. 2. If you meet a person who looks like you but smiles too widely — that is not you. 3. If the fog begins to take on a pinkish tint, close your eyes and do not breathe for three minutes. 4. Remember: the exit is where you least want to be.'
225: I found a tree in the forest where children's shoes hung instead of leaves. They were all different sizes and colors, but they all had one common detail — the laces were tied together to form a giant loop around the trunk. When the wind blew, the shoes started knocking against each other, creating a rhythm like a tap dance performed by someone invisible and very heavy.
226: My pulse has started transmitting messages in Morse code. This morning it tapped out: "THEY ARE INSIDE YOUR EYES." I spent half an hour in front of the mirror trying to see something under my pupils, and at one point I thought I saw someone tiny waving to me from the darkness deep inside. Now I'm afraid to blink; I fear that while I'm blinking, they might seize control of my vision.
227: Found a key to room 0 in an old hotel. The hotel only has three floors and the rooms start from 101. When I inserted the key into the wall between two doors, a passage opened into a room filled with my childhood toys. But they were all alive: the teddy bear was breathing, and the dolls were whispering about how I left them in a box years ago. They looked very offended, and the largest rabbit held a real kitchen knife in its paws.
228: Note on the fridge: 'Don't eat the meat in the freezer. It isn't beef. It's what's left of your ability to empathize. If you cook it, you will never be able to cry again, but you will start to understand the language of insects. Decide for yourself what is more important — human feelings or knowing what the flies are buzzing about over the corpses in the ditch.'
229: Yesterday I saw the sky crack like old plaster, and behind it wasn't the void of space, but a boundless wall of dirty concrete with photos of missing people glued to it. It turns out our world is just a box decorated on the inside, and beyond it lies the real Silent Hill — an endless construction site where monster-workers build labyrinths for our souls.
230: I found an old lighter in a desk drawer. When I light it, the flame burns downward, not upward, and in its light, things are visible that aren't there in normal lighting: inscriptions on the walls made in invisible ink, and threads stretching from my fingers to the ceiling. Yesterday, in the light of this lighter, I saw a tiny creature with my ex-wife's face sitting on my shoulder, constantly whispering all my mistakes into my ear.
231: Today on the pier I met an old man drawing a door on the asphalt with chalk. When he finished, he knocked on the drawing, and the door opened. He stepped inside and disappeared, and the drawing was immediately washed away by a sudden rain. I tried to draw the same door, but all I got was a crooked window from which a chill and the smell of old newspapers wafted. Apparently, I don't have enough imagination to escape this prison.
232: At the pharmacy, they sold me eye drops called "Truth." The instructions said: "Apply one drop to see the world as it really is." I took the risk. The world turned into a web of rusty pipes and pulsating flesh. The people around me turned out to be just heaps of meat dressed in clothes, and the buildings were giant skeletons draped in stone. But the most terrifying thing was the sky — it had turned into a giant eyelid that was slowly closing.
233: Note in an abandoned cafe: 'If the waitress offers you the "special menu," politely decline. This menu includes dishes made from your unfulfilled dreams. It tastes like ash and tears, but after eating, you will forever lose the desire to achieve anything. You will become like us — shadows that just sit here and wait for this endless day to end.'
234: My shadow this morning began to reflect on the wall separately from me. It lived its own life: drinking imaginary coffee, reading an invisible newspaper, and even trying to strangle the shadow of a passing cat. When I tried to approach it, it wagged a finger at me and pointed to the exit. It seems even my own shadow thinks I don't belong here and wants me to leave while I still can.
235: Found an old tape recorder in the basement of Alchemilla Hospital. On the tape was a psychotherapy session: "Doctor, I'm not afraid of the dark. I'm afraid that the darkness is starting to recognize me. Yesterday it called me by name and asked to borrow my eyes for a couple of hours. I refused, but today I woke up to find my pupils have gone completely white, and a lump of darkness is standing in the corner of the room, looking at me with my own eyes."
236: Today I discovered that my apartment has one more door than it had yesterday. It's behind the wardrobe and leads to a room that exactly replicates mine, but everything in it is made of paper. A paper bed, a paper table, even a paper version of myself lying on the floor. When I entered, the paper me tried to scream, but instead of sound, confetti poured from his mouth. I quickly closed the door and pushed the wardrobe back.
237: Yesterday in the fog I found an old tram car. There were no passengers inside, just rows of empty seats covered in dust. But when I sat down, the car started moving, even though there were no rails beneath it. We drove through a void, and frames of my life that I wanted to forget flashed outside the windows. The car stopped at a building that looked like my kindergarten, but thick black smoke was coming from the windows, and headless dolls hung on the fence.
238: Note taped to the TV: 'Don't switch to channel 0. They show a live broadcast from hell there, and the cameraman is you. If you see yourself there, it means your soul has already begun its transformation. Better turn off the TV and smash the screen with a hammer before the image starts coming out and filling the room with a black liquid that smells of burnt plastic.'
239: I found an old well in the woods. If you shout your name into it, it answers with the name of the person you will kill in the future. I shouted "James," and the well answered "Mary." I don't know any Mary, but now I'm afraid to meet new people. What if this city has already written my role in a script I don't want to play?
240: Today my fingers grew two centimeters longer. The skin on them stretched thin like parchment. I feel my hands turning into something capable only of climbing walls or strangling. The doctors in this city (the ones with bandages for faces) say this is a sign of "spiritual growth" and soon I will be able to reach the sky itself, if it exists at all.
241: In the amusement park, I went into the "Hall of Mirrors," but all the mirrors there showed me at the moments of my greatest humiliations. In one mirror, I was crying at a funeral; in another, I was committing a foul deed for profit. I didn't laugh. I ran for the exit, but all the doors led back to the hall of mirrors. Now I've been sitting here for an eternity, looking at how ugly I truly am inside.
242: Note under my car's windshield wiper: 'Your car won't go anywhere anymore. The roads in this city only lead in circles. If you try to leave, you'll just see the same gas stations and abandoned motels passing by the window. Better burn it. Fire is the only way to attract the attention of those who live in the sky, though I doubt they care about us.'
243: Today I found a plate of apples on the kitchen table, but when I took one, it turned out to be made of human flesh. Inside, instead of seeds, were small teeth. The strangest thing is that I felt an uncontrollable urge to eat it. The city is gradually changing my tastes, habituating me to things that used to make me nauseous. I'm afraid I'll soon stop distinguishing food from remains.
244: In the library, I found a city map where all the streets are named after my fears: "Loneliness Dead-end," "Betrayal Avenue," "Lost Child Lane." The largest square is called "The Square of Void." I am exactly there right now, and there truly is nothing here — no buildings, no roads, just me and the endless gray asphalt stretching into the fog.
245: My alarm clock rang today in the voice of my mother, who died five years ago. She said: "Get up, it's time for the funeral." I asked: "Whose?" — and she replied: "Yours, of course. Everyone has already gathered; don't keep people waiting." After that, the clock smoked and melted, leaving a puddle of black metal on the nightstand that looked like a frozen tear.
246: Note on the morgue door: 'Please close the refrigeration units more tightly. The dead are complaining about drafts. Yesterday one of them came into the hallway to ask for a blanket and scared the night shift to death. Be merciful to those who have already suffered. They also need a little comfort in their eternal wait for a worthless resurrection.'
247: Yesterday I found an old video camera. When I looked through the viewfinder, I saw the world in infrared. Everything living glowed bright red, but in the fog, I saw giant blue figures moving slowly between the houses. They were cold as ice and had no faces, only giant funnels for heads. It seems they are the true masters of Silent Hill, and we are just parasites on their bodies.
248: My cat spoke to me today. She said she sees creatures crawling on my bedroom ceiling while I sleep. She described them as long black threads with children's faces. She advised me not to open my mouth in my sleep, otherwise they might crawl inside and replace my thoughts with theirs. Now I tape my mouth shut before going to bed.
249: I found an old suit in the basement that fit me perfectly. But when I put it on, I realized I couldn't take it off. It started merging with my skin, and now I feel the fabric growing fibers into my muscles. The strangest thing is that I feel much more confident in this suit. It seems I'm becoming someone else, better suited for this place — a faceless extra in the background of a nightmare.
250: Note found in a bottle on the shore of Lake Toluca: 'The water in this lake is not water, but the molten memory of all the drowned. If you drink it, you will learn the secrets of the city, but your tongue will forever turn into a piece of rusty iron. I drank. Now I know where the key to heaven is hidden, but I cannot name it because my mouth is full of blood and metal. Don't repeat my mistake, stranger.'
251: Today I found an old typewriter. As soon as I inserted a sheet, it started typing on its own: "James, why did you come here? You know she isn't coming back. You just want to be punished for what you did." I tried to pull the sheet out, but the carriage struck my fingers, and the machine continued: "Your sins are the only thing connecting you to reality. Without them, you are nothing."
252: At an abandoned gas station, I saw a map marked with "Exit from Silent Hill." I drove the indicated route, but the road led me to a huge mirror placed in the middle of the highway. In the mirror, I saw my car driving backward, deeper into the fog. I realized the exit exists only in my imagination, and reality is an endless loop tied in a knot around my throat.
253: Yesterday I went into an antique shop, and the owner offered to sell me my own old watch that I lost as a child. When I wound it up, time in the shop went backward: it became light outside, the fog vanished, and I saw my mother standing on the street. But the moment I let go of the winding crown, everything went back, and the watch turned into a handful of sand in my hand.
254: Note on the hospital bathroom wall: 'If you see blood flowing from the tap — it's normal. If you see fingers trying to crawl out of the drain — it's also normal. But if you hear your reflection start to laugh when you're sad — run out of this room as fast as you can. It means your double is ready to take your place in this world.'
255: Today I found an abandoned altar in the woods with a fresh red apple on it. When I cut it open, there was a human eye inside that kept blinking. Instead of juice, thick warm blood flowed from the apple. I heard a whisper from behind the trees: "Accept the city's gift, and it will stop tormenting your memory." I left the apple and walked away, but the smell of blood follows me even now.
256: My pulse today is rhythmically tapping out the melody my mother sang to me in a lullaby. But with every beat, the music becomes more distorted until it turns into a metallic grating. I feel my heart is gradually being replaced by a rusty mechanism that runs not on blood, but on my fear. Soon I'll become just another clockwork toy in this foggy theater.
257: Yesterday I saw a man walking down the street who had a television instead of a head. My own dreams were being broadcast on the screen. All the onlookers (monsters with sewn mouths) stopped and watched the screen, nodding their heads. I realized there is no privacy in this city — even your subconscious belongs to the public if that public is hungry enough for your nightmares.
258: Note taped to the inside of my apartment door: 'Don't go outside today. The fog has grown too hungry. Yesterday it ate the mailman right before my eyes — the man just dissolved, leaving only a bag of letters. Today the fog smells of fresh meat and is waiting for you to open the door. Better sit in the dark and pretend you're not home. Maybe it will find another victim.'
259: I found a lock of hair tied with a black ribbon in an old dresser. When I touched it, I felt a sharp pain in the back of my head, as if someone had yanked my hair. Now I constantly feel someone's presence behind my back, and when I turn around, I see only the tip of a long black strand disappearing into the corner. It seems I found part of someone who really wants to be whole again.
260: Today a damp patch appeared on the bedroom wall that takes the shape of a map of Silent Hill. If you press your ear to it, you can hear the noise of the city: siren sounds, the screech of metal, and someone's distant crying. The most terrifying part is that the patch is slowly growing, and today a small red dot appeared on it — the place where I am now. And black cracks are reaching toward this dot from all sides.
261: Yesterday I found an old doll maker in an abandoned toy store. He sat in the corner sewing human fingers to porcelain bodies. When he saw me, he smiled and said: "Oh, you have perfect joints. Would you like to donate them for art? In return, I'll give you immortality in the form of a beautiful doll that will never feel pain." I ran away, but my knees now click strangely with every step.
262: Note in the Lakeside Hotel elevator: 'If the elevator stops between floors, do not press the call button. Just wait. A man with a pyramid for a head will enter. He won't harm you if you don't look him in the eye (though he has none). He just wants to ride a few floors down, to where reality becomes liquid. When he exits, close your eyes and count to a hundred. The elevator will take you back.'
263: Today I found a jar in the fridge labeled "Your Uncried Tears." When I opened it, salt water splashed out and instantly filled the entire kitchen. I started drowning in my own emotions that I had suppressed for years. The water was icy and smelled of loneliness. I barely managed to swim into the hallway before the kitchen door slammed and locked itself.
264: Yesterday I saw the trees in the forest start to tear their roots from the ground and crawl slowly closer to the city. They whispered with their dry leaves: "We're coming for you, James. You can't hide in the fog. We will become the walls of your cage, and you will never see the sun." It seems even nature in this place has conspired against my sanity.
265: Note on an old typewriter in a newspaper office: 'Main news of the day — you're still here. Main news of tomorrow — you're already gone. Reporting from the scene: the fog has swallowed the last hope of a city resident. Read in the latest issue: how to go insane correctly without attracting the attention of pyramid-headed executioners. The price of the paper — your left kidney or the right to oblivion.'
266: Today I found an old mirror in the attic that shows not me, but what I would be if I had never made mistakes. That other me in the mirror is happy; he has a family and light in his eyes. He looked at me with such infinite regret that I couldn't take it and smashed the glass. But the shards continue to show his happy face, only now it's all in cracks and blood is flowing from them.
267: Yesterday I went into a church, but instead of icons, giant meat carcasses dressed in clerical robes hung there. The priest (a creature with sewn eyes) preached that suffering is the only path to salvation. He said the city is purgatory and we should be grateful for every drop of pain because it proves we still exist. At the end, he offered me communion with rusty nails.
268: Note under a pillow in the motel: 'Don't sleep on your right side. On your left side, you dream of the past; on your right side, you dream of what the city will do to you tomorrow. Yesterday I accidentally slept on my right side all night and now I know what my own death smells like. It's the smell of damp earth and the cheap cologne I wore on our wedding day. Better not to sleep at all if you want to keep your wits.'
269: Today I discovered that my skin has begun to turn into a canvas. Tattoos are appearing on my arms by themselves, depicting scenes from my life that I’ve never told anyone about. The drawings are very detailed and painful; they emerge through the flesh like burns. Mary's face is slowly forming on my chest right now, and I feel her lips on my skin beginning to move, voicing accusations.
270: Yesterday I found an abandoned playground in the woods. The swings were moving by themselves, and ghostly figures of children sat on them. When they saw me, they stopped playing and began to point their fingers at me, chanting in unison: "Killer, killer, killer." I tried to run away, but the sand under my feet turned into a sticky mass resembling decomposed flesh, and I barely escaped alive.
271: Note on the control panel in an abandoned bowling alley: 'Game over. You knocked down the wrong pins. Every pin was someone's hope, and the ball was your egoism. Now you'll have to collect the fragments of your dreams all over the city. And remember: there are no prizes in this game, only penalties in the form of extra years spent in this foggy hell. Your score is an infinity of negative emotions.'
272: Today I found an old recipe book. One of them was called "Remorse Soup." Ingredients: a handful of ash from burned letters, two cups of bitter tears, three drops of a traitor's blood, and a pinch of earth from a loved one's grave. Simmer until the aroma makes you remember everything you tried to forget. I cooked it. Now I can't stop hearing her voice in my head.
273: Yesterday I went into a public restroom and saw that all the stalls were occupied by creatures reading newspapers from the future. One of them looked at me and said: "Oh, you're just in time. Your obituary was just printed on page three. Want to read? It says you died of boredom and self-pity in an empty motel room." I refused and ran outside, but the smell of printer's ink follows me everywhere.
274: Note on the mirror in a barber shop: 'We will cut not only your hair but all your excess memories. Our razor is so sharp it can sever guilt or attachment to the past. After our haircut, you will become light as air and empty as this city. Don't be alarmed if gray fog comes out of the cuts instead of blood — it's just a sign that you have finally been cleansed of humanity.'
275: Today I found an abandoned bus in the woods. Inside sat skeletons dressed in festive attire. A map was lying on the driver's lap, with the route "Heaven — Silent Hill" marked on it. A one-way ticket was clenched in the teeth of one of the passengers. The ticket said: "Enjoy the ride; no return trips provided due to lack of arrival destination." I got off the bus, and it immediately dissolved into the fog.
276: My watch today started ticking in the rhythm of my fading heart. Every time the hand takes a step, I feel a cold prick in my chest. I realized that time in this city is not a physical quantity, but a measure of the exhaustion of my soul. When the watch stops, only an empty shell will remain of me, which the city will fill with fog and rust, turning me into another silent inhabitant of its streets.
277: Yesterday I found an old typewriter in the basement that types with teeth instead of letters. Every key strike leaves a clear imprint of a human incisor or molar on the paper. Today it typed an entire page that looks like a terrifying grin. I'm afraid to touch the keys; I feel that if I make a typo, it will bite off my finger as punishment for illiteracy.
278: Note in an abandoned electronics store: 'All our TVs show only one film — "Your Life: Uncensored Version." Starring everyone you ever hurt. The script is written by your conscience, the director is a demon from your nightmares. Admission is free, but the exit costs half your sanity. Enjoy the show, provided you're brave enough to watch until the final credits.'
279: Today I met a little girl on the street playing hopscotch on the sidewalk. But instead of numbers in the squares, the dates of death of my loved ones were written. She jumped from one date to another, singing: "Hop-skip, to the coffin-lock, who didn't hide — gets soaked in the fog." When she hopped to the date of my death (which hasn't happened yet), she stopped, looked at me, and vanished, leaving only a wet footprint on the asphalt.
280: Yesterday I found an abandoned drive-in theater in the woods. Frames of my life were being broadcast on the screen, but in slow motion and with commentary in Latin. A voiceover analyzed my every action as a crime against the universe. I tried to cover my ears, but the sound came from right inside my head. The film ended with a scene of me standing before this very screen watching this very film. An endless recursion of guilt.
281: Note on an old payphone: 'If you need to call the past, press 1. If the future — 2. If you want to talk to someone you killed — press 0 and wait an eternity. Remember: the rate per minute of conversation is one year of your life. We do not accept credit cards, only cash in the form of your sincere tears and pieces of a broken heart. The connection may drop at any moment due to interference in your conscience.'
282: Today I discovered that my shadows (yes, there are three now) have started arguing among themselves. One wants me to surrender to the city, the second wants me to keep fighting, and the third just stays silent and draws a noose on the floor. The most terrifying part is they've become material: yesterday one of them pushed me, and I fell, scraping my knee. It seems my internal conflicts have taken physical form and are now trying to decide my fate without my involvement.
283: Yesterday I went into an abandoned library and found a book titled "How to Stop Existing in 10 Simple Steps." The first step was: "Forget your name." The second: "Stop reflecting in mirrors." I reached step five: "Start breathing fog instead of air," and realized I was already halfway to the end. The book was written in my handwriting, but I don't remember ever writing it. Or maybe I just already forgot?
284: Note on the door of an empty ward in Brookhaven Hospital: 'Patient transferred to the "Nowhere" department. Reason: total loss of contact with reality. He claims the city is a living organism that feeds on our suffering. Yesterday he tried to feed the wall his arm. The walls accepted the offering. Only a bed and the smell of formalin remain in the ward. Do not go inside; the walls are still hungry and waiting for seconds.'
285: Today I found an old photo of Mary. But when I looked at it, her face on the print began to slowly rot. The skin blackened, the eyes flowed out, until only a bare skull remained on the photo, continuing to smile at me. I tried to tear the photo, but it felt hard as metal and cut my fingers. Blood from the cut hit the photo, and the skull on it began to greedily lick it up, emitting a satisfied purring sound.
286: Yesterday in the fog I met a man carrying a giant sack on his shoulders. Cries and pleas for help came from the sack. I asked him what was inside, and he replied: "These are all my unfulfilled promises. They've become so heavy I can't stand straight. Want to take one? I see the sack on your back isn't that big yet; there's room." I looked at my shoulders and saw that I also had a sack I hadn't noticed before.
287: Note under the lid of an old piano: 'Don't play a minor scale. It summons the ghosts of those who died of melancholy in this house. Yesterday I risked it, and creatures resembling wet rags with human eyes began to crawl out of the corners. They started dancing to the music, and with every bar, I felt life leaving my fingers. Better play something cheerful, though in this city, cheerful music sounds like a mockery of the dead.'
288: Today I discovered that my apartment has one wall less. Instead, an opening now leads to an infinite staircase going up into a gray void. I tried to climb a few steps, but with every step, I became older: my hands were covered in wrinkles and my vision weakened. I realized this staircase is my life path, and if I reach the top, I will simply crumble into dust. I went back, but the wall did not reappear.
289: Yesterday I found an abandoned mail van in the woods. Inside were thousands of letters addressed to me. They were all from people I used to know, and all had the same text: "Why did you abandon us? Why did you choose this fog over us? We're waiting for you at home, but home is now here, in your memory which you are slowly killing." I burned the letters, but the smoke from them turned into the faces of my friends, looking at me with hatred.
290: Note on an old radio in the police station: 'We caught a signal from the abyss. It says Silent Hill isn't a city, but a giant mirror God looks into when He wants to see His own madness. We are just bacteria on the surface of that mirror. If God blinks, we vanish. If He cries, we are flooded with blood. We recommend all staff to pray, but remember: your prayers here sound like blasphemy.'
291: Today I found an old doll without a head. When I picked it up, it started speaking in my voice, telling my most secret secrets. It knew everything: my fears, my sins, what I did to Mary. I tried to plug its mouth, but the doll had no mouth — the sound came from right inside its empty body. I threw it into a well, but the voice continued to sound from deep in the earth for several hours until I ran from the forest.
292: Yesterday in the fog I saw a building that looked like a replica of my childhood home. I went inside and saw my family sitting at the table. They acted as if I had never left. But when I moved closer, I saw they all had black holes instead of eyes, with flies flying out. They offered me to sit and eat "dinner," which consisted of raw earth and broken glass. I jumped out the window and discovered the building was gone.
293: Note on the dashboard of an abandoned boat: 'Don't try to cross the lake. In its depths lives the God of Silent Hill, and He very much dislikes being disturbed during His sleep. Yesterday my friends' boat flipped by itself in the middle of the lake, and giant hands rose from the water to drag them to the bottom. The water in the lake is liquid suffering, and if you fall in, you'll become part of its eternal cold. Stay on the shore and wait for your hour.'
294: Today I discovered my teeth have started changing: they've become sharp and jagged like a shark's. I feel constant hunger, but normal food tastes like flavorless grass to me. Yesterday I caught myself looking with longing at my own hand. The city wants to turn me into one of those monsters wandering its streets, and I feel my humanity surrendering without a fight, yielding to the primal instincts of a predator.
295: Yesterday I found an abandoned tent in the woods. Inside was a hiker's diary, the last entries written in blood: "The fog has started imitating the scent of my wife. I know she's at home in Seattle, but here it smells of her perfume and fresh coffee. I'm afraid to go out because someone is standing outside the tent scratching their claws against the fabric, whispering in my voice: 'Let us in, we've brought you forgiveness.' I don't believe them. I don't believe myself."
296: Note on the wall of an old cinema: 'The screening of "End of the World" is postponed indefinitely due to a lack of viewers. All potential witnesses have already become part of the scenery. If you are reading this, you are the last actor in this theater of the absurd. Your task is to die beautifully in the final scene so the city can finally close for major renovations. The script is under your seat; don't forget to learn your last words.'
297: Today I found an old key on the street with a keychain that had my name on it. I started looking for the door it opens and went all over the city. Eventually, I found a small door in the wall of the city hospital. When I opened it, I saw a room crammed to the ceiling with my childhood photos, which had been slashed with a knife. In the center stood a coffin my size, and inside lay a note: "We've been waiting for you, James. Your place has already grown cold."
298: Yesterday I saw a giant cloud in the shape of Mary's face float across the sky. It looked at the city with such infinite sadness that a rain of black tears began. These tears burned through clothes and left painful marks on the skin like a brand. I realized the city isn't just my nightmare, but her prison too, locked by my memories and my guilt. We are both captives of this place, and there is no way out.
299: Note under a mat in the motel: 'If you hear the siren — don't run. It doesn't warn of danger; it invites it into your world. With every sound of the siren, reality changes: walls are covered in rust, and people turn into monsters. This is the heartbeat of the city, and you must dance to it if you don't want to be crushed by the weight of the falling sky. Close your eyes and imagine it's just a bad dream. But remember: people don't wake up from this dream.'
300: I finally realized that Silent Hill isn't a place on a map. It's a state of a soul pushed to the limit. The fog is my doubt, the monsters are my sins, and the rust is my decay. I cannot leave here because I *am* this city. Every building is my neuron, every street is my vein. I am trapped inside myself, and this nightmare will last forever until I learn to forgive myself. But in this city, forgiveness does not exist. Only punishment.
